note: Verify pass 2026-09-11. passcheck had only one Wikidata lead (an Anne Frank sapling, not chased) and no register. Found the naming body: City of Pittsburgh Shade Tree Commission's 'Remarkable Trees of Pittsburgh' program (partnership with Tree Pittsburgh), confirmed via official meeting minutes (a real government PDF). remarkabletreespgh.com itself, which almost certainly has the full designated list with better detail and photos, is JavaScript-rendered and returned nothing to plain curl or WebFetch this pass; a browser-rendering pass should retry it directly and would likely upgrade all four delivered trees plus surface more. 4 trees delivered (pit_001-004), reaching the 4-tree floor. Pass 2026-10-22: the program's Google My Map KML gave 16 tree points; 12 new trees delivered to data/research/pittsburgh-verified.json (pit_005-016) from Shade Tree Commission minutes 2023-03-16 and 2024-03-21 plus the map coordinates. All one-source (government minutes), no girth or age published anywhere.

leads.name: Pin upgrade for pit_001 to pit_004 (Mellon Park cypress, katsura, lacebark pine, Phillips Park white oak)
leads.why: The Remarkable Trees map has tree-level points: Mellon bald cypress 40.45177,-79.91696; katsura 40.4522,-79.91681; lacebark pine 40.45465,-79.9145; Phillips Park white oak 40.39147,-79.9917 (current pins 40.4535,-79.9168 / 40.4548,-79.9168 / 40.3906,-79.9916). Cypress and katsura are about 100 m from the current pin and the lacebark pine is 190 m off. Official tree-level evidence for pin_source; apply as a pin move.

leads.why: Not on the map and not in the 2024 designations; no point or update found. The 2024 Champion elm is in Allegheny Commons (pit_011), a different tree.
